narrative:
The model gave your application a 63% likelihood of bad credit, meaning that among applicants with a similar profile, about two in three are expected to struggle with repayment. Because this is above the bank’s risk limit, your loan was denied. Your sex, age, and foreign-worker status did not influence this decision.

The strongest reason was your checking account status. A balance between 0 and 200 DM was treated as a warning sign rather than a strength, and it was the leading factor pushing the prediction toward bad credit. Next came your property situation. Having no property recorded is uncommon among approved applicants—only about 8% fall into that group—and it suggests fewer assets the bank could rely on if payments become difficult. The third major factor was the requested term: asking for 36 months is well above the approved average of about 19 months, so the bank sees a longer period of uncertainty.

Other details, such as your requested amount of 4,795 DM versus an average near 3,020 DM and an installment rate of 4% versus about 3%, add to the cautious picture.

To improve a future application, consider requesting less money over a shorter period, building a stronger savings balance, providing a guarantor or collateral, and documenting stable employment. You can also ask the bank what specific changes would make your profile acceptable before reapplying.
